extracted.intended_audience: users of the SINGULAR computer algebra system (mathematicians and programmers using SINGULAR)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for SINGULAR Chapter 5: Functions and system variables — describes syntax, types, purposes, notes and examples for built-in procedures and options.

rubrics_metrics.name: max
rubrics_metrics.description: returns the maximum for any arguments of a type for which '>' is defined
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: max (i1, ..., ik). Type: same as type of i1,...,ik respectively. Examples: max(2,3) -> 3; max(1,4,3) -> 4; max on intvec compares lexicographically; on polynomials returns polynomial with biggest leading monomial. See also min.

rubrics_metrics.name: maxideal
rubrics_metrics.description: returns the power given by int expression of the maximal ideal generated by all ring variables (maxideal(i)=1 for i<=0)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: maxideal ( int expression ). Type: ideal. Example: ring r=32003,(x,y,z),dp; maxideal(2); returns generators for the square of the maximal ideal. See Section 4.5 [ideal], Section 4.19 [ring].

rubrics_metrics.name: memory
rubrics_metrics.description: returns statistics concerning the memory management: memory(0) active bytes, memory(1) bytes allocated from OS, memory(2) maximal bytes ever allocated during session
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: memory ( int expression ). Type: bigint. Note: to monitor memory usage during computations set option(mem). Example shows usage in a ReportMemoryUsage procedure and how memory changes after killing objects. See option(mem) and Section 5.1.108 [option].

rubrics_metrics.name: min
rubrics_metrics.description: documented as 'Procedure from library standard.lib' but content in this chunk repeats max's description (returns the maximum for any arguments of a type for which '>' is defined)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax and examples appear to mirror the 'max' entry in this chunk. See Section 5.1.88 [min] (page 218) for the correct 'min' documentation and relation to max.

rubrics_metrics.name: minbase
rubrics_metrics.description: returns a minimal set of generators of an ideal or module if the input is homogeneous or if the ordering is local
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: minbase ( ideal expression ) or minbase ( module expression ). Type: same as input. Note: not available over coefficient rings. Example shows usage with homogeneous ideals and relation to mstd. See Section 5.1.97 [mstd].

rubrics_metrics.name: minor
rubrics_metrics.description: returns the specified set of (mSize x mSize)-minors (subdeterminants) of a given matrix as generators of an ideal
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: minor ( matrix expression M, int expression mSize, [ ideal expression I], [ int expression k], [ string expression algorithm], [ int expression cachedP], [ int expression cachedM]). Type: ideal. Notes: If optional I given, computations are modulo I; parameter k controls how many minors (positive k = first k non-zero minors, negative k = first |k| minors regardless of zero); ordering among minors only guaranteed when k<>0; algorithm can be B/bareiss, L/laplace, or C/cache; defaults for cacheP and cacheM are 200 and 100000 for C/cache. Behavior: returns 0 if mSize larger than matrix, returns 1 if mSize<1. Examples demonstrate computing all 2x2 minors and first k minors modulo an ideal and with Laplace algorithm. See det.

rubrics_metrics.name: minres
rubrics_metrics.description: minimizes a free resolution of an ideal or module given by a list expression or resolution expression
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: minres ( list expression ) or minres ( resolution expression ). Type: list or resolution accordingly. Purpose: reduces a resolution to a minimal one. Example shows computing resolution rs=lres(i,0) then minres(rs). See related commands lres, mres, res, sres.

rubrics_metrics.name: modulo
rubrics_metrics.description: represents h1/(h1 ∩ h2) ∼= (h1 + h2)/h2 where h1 and h2 are submodules of the same free module; returns generators of the kernel of the induced map
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: modulo ( ideal expression, ideal expression ) or modulo ( module expression, module expression ). Type: module. Notes: If one of h1 or h2 has attribute isHomog set and weights compatible, modulo sets isHomog. Example given with ideals h1=x,y,z and h2=x producing generators for the module modulo(h1,h2). See hom kernel and syz.

rubrics_metrics.name: monitor
rubrics_metrics.description: controls recording of user input and/or program output into a file; second argument describes what to log: 'i' input, 'o' output, 'io' both; default 'i'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: monitor ( link expression ) or monitor ( link expression, string expression ). Type: none. Each monitor command closes previous monitor file and opens given file; monitor("") turns off recording. Example: monitor("doe.tmp","io"); ... monitor("") stops logging; doe.tmp contains the recorded input/output. See link expressions.

rubrics_metrics.name: monomial
rubrics_metrics.description: converts an integer vector to a power product (inverse to leadexp); returns a vector if length of argument equals number of variables + 1
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: monomial ( intvec expression ). Type: poly or vector. Example: monomial(intvec(2,3)) -> x^2 y^3; monomial(intvec(2,3,0,1)) -> x^2 y^3 * gen(1); leadexp(monomial(...)) recovers the intvec. See intvec and leadexp.

rubrics_metrics.name: mpresmat
rubrics_metrics.description: computes the multipolynomial resultant matrix of the input system using either sparse resultant matrix method (Gelfand-Kapranov-Zelevinsky) or Macaulay resultant matrix method
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: mpresmat ( ideal expression, int expression ). Type: module. Note: For Macaulay method (param=1) input system must be homogeneous and number of polynomials must be number of base-ring variables plus one. Example demonstrates building resultant matrix for a given system and printing it. See uressolve.

rubrics_metrics.name: mres
rubrics_metrics.description: computes a minimal free resolution of an ideal or module M with the standard basis method
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: mres ( ideal expression, int expression ) or mres ( module expression, int expression ). Type: resolution. Purpose: computes free resolution of coker(A) where A=matrix(M); if int expression k != 0, stops after k steps and returns list of modules; mres(M,0) returns at most n+2 modules (n = number of variables). Note: accessing single elements may trigger partial computations and take time. Example shows computing resolution and reading projective dimension. See fres, hres, lres, res, sres.

rubrics_metrics.name: mstd
rubrics_metrics.description: returns a list whose first entry is a standard basis for the ideal/module and whose second entry is a generating set; if coefficient ring is a field and ideal/module is homogeneous or ordering is local, the second entry is a minimal generating set
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: mstd ( ideal expression ) or mstd ( module expression ). Type: list. Example given for a Jacobian ideal, showing returned standard basis and generating set. See ideal, minbase, module, std.

rubrics_metrics.name: mult
rubrics_metrics.description: computes the degree of the monomial ideal/module generated by the leading monomials of the input; if input is a standard basis of a homogeneous ideal returns the degree; in a local ring with local degree ordering returns multiplicity (Samuel multiplicity)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: mult ( ideal expression ) or mult ( module expression ). Type: int. Examples show computing mult(std(jacob(f))) and mult(std(f)). See degree, dim, std, vdim.

rubrics_metrics.name: nameof
rubrics_metrics.description: returns the name of an expression as string
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: nameof ( expression ). Type: string. Example: int i=9; string s=nameof(i); -> 'i'. nameof(i+1) returns empty string. nameof(basering) returns 'basering' if basering is defined; examples show error if basering undefined and proper behaviour after ring r; related to names and reservedName/typeof.

rubrics_metrics.name: names
rubrics_metrics.description: returns the names of all user-defined variables which are ring independent, or names belonging to given ring or level
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: names(), names(ring name), names(package name), names(level). Type: list of strings. Purpose: returns names of user-defined variables (including procedures) which are ring independent or belong to given ring; third case restricts by level. Example shows names() and names(r) outputs; package can be Current, Top, etc. See nameof and reservedName.

rubrics_metrics.name: ncols
rubrics_metrics.description: returns the number of columns of a matrix, an intmat, or the number of given generators of the ideal, including zeros
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: ncols ( matrix expression ) | ncols ( intmat expression ) | ncols ( ideal expression ). Type: int. Note: size(ideal) counts number of generators different from zero; use nrows to get matrix rows. Examples: ncols on a 5x6 matrix returns 6; ncols(ideal i=x,0,y) -> 3 while size(i) -> 2. See matrix, nrows, size.

rubrics_metrics.name: npars
rubrics_metrics.description: returns the number of parameters of a ring
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: npars ( ring name ). Type: int. Example: ring r=(23,t,v),(x,a(1..7)),lp; npars(r) -> 2. See par, parstr, ring.

rubrics_metrics.name: nres
rubrics_metrics.description: computes a free resolution of an ideal or module M which is minimized from the second module on (by standard basis method)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: nres ( ideal expression, int expression ) or nres ( module expression, int expression ). Type: resolution. Purpose and structure of resolution similar to mres but L[1]=M identical to input and L[2] minimal generators for first syzygy, etc. If int expression k != 0, stops after k steps. Example shows nres(M,0) and note 'resolution not minimized yet' in intermediate output. See fres, hres, mres, res, sres.

rubrics_metrics.name: nrows
rubrics_metrics.description: returns the number of rows of a matrix, an intmat or intvec, or the minimal rank of a free module in which the given module or vector lives (index of last non-zero component)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: nrows ( matrix expression ) | nrows ( intmat expression ) | nrows ( intvec expression ) | nrows ( module expression ) | nrows ( vector expression ). Type: int. Note: use ncols to get number of columns. Examples: nrows(M) for 2x3 matrix -> 2; nrows(freemodule(4)) -> 4; nrows([0,x,0]) -> 2. See gen, matrix, module, ncols, vector.

rubrics_metrics.name: numerator
rubrics_metrics.description: returns the numerator of a number
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: numerator ( number expression ). Type: number. Example: number n = 3/2; numerator(n) -> 3. See cleardenom, content, denominator.

rubrics_metrics.name: nvars
rubrics_metrics.description: returns the number of variables of a ring
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: nvars ( ring name ). Type: int. Example: ring r=(23,t,v),(x,a(1..7)),ls; nvars(r) -> 8. See npars, ring, var, varstr.

rubrics_metrics.name: open
rubrics_metrics.description: opens a link
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: open ( link expression ). Type: none. Example: link l="ssi:tcp localhost:"+system("Singular"); open(l); // start SINGULAR 'server' on localhost in batchmode; close(l) to shut down. See close and link.

rubrics_metrics.name: option
rubrics_metrics.description: lists, sets, dumps, or restores options that manipulate behavior of computations and output; disabling an option uses prefix 'no'; some options are set via direct assignment rather than option()
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple syntaxes: option() returns string of defined options; option(option name) sets an option; option(get) returns intvec state of options; option(set,intvec) restores state. Use prefix 'no' to disable. Many boolean options control standard-basis and other algorithm strategies (none, warn, returnSB, fastHC, infRedTail, intStrategy, lazy, length, notRegularity, notSugar, notBuckets, prot, qringNF, redSB, redTail, redThrough, sugarCrit, weightM, cancelunit, contentSB, intersectElim, intersectSyz, etc.). Special numeric-assigned options: multBound and degBound (reset by assigning 0). Output control options: Imap, debugLib, defRes, loadLib, loadProc, mem, notWarnSB, prompt, reading, redefine, usage. Examples show toggling options, using option(get)/option(set) and interpreting option(prot) protocol characters for many computations (facstd, fglm, groebner, lres, mres, minres, mstd, res, slimgb, sres, std, stdfglm, stdhilb, syz, etc.) and detailed meanings of protocol characters. See degBound, multBound, std.

rubrics_metrics.name: ord
rubrics_metrics.description: returns the (weighted) degree of the initial term of a polynomial or vector; weights are those used for first block of ring ordering
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: ord ( poly expression ) or ord ( vector expression ). Type: int. Note: ord(0) is -1; in a global degree ordering ord equals deg. Examples show ord and deg for weighted and weighted-sum orderings and for vectors. See deg, poly, vector.

rubrics_metrics.name: ordstr
rubrics_metrics.description: returns the description of the monomial ordering of the ring as a string
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: ordstr ( ring name ). Type: string. Example: ring r=7,(x,y),wp(2,3); ordstr(r) -> 'wp(2,3),C'. See charstr, parstr, ring, varstr.

rubrics_metrics.name: par
rubrics_metrics.description: par(n) returns the n-th parameter of the basering
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: par ( int expression ). Type: number. Example: ring r=(0,a,b,c),(x,y,z),dp; par(2) -> (b). See char, npars, parstr, ring.

rubrics_metrics.name: pardeg
rubrics_metrics.description: returns the degree of a number considered as a polynomial in the ring parameters
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: pardeg ( number expression ). Type: int. Example: ring r=(0,a,b,c),(x,y,z),dp; pardeg(a^2*b) -> 3. See deg, number, ring.

rubrics_metrics.name: parstr
rubrics_metrics.description: returns the list of parameters of the ring as a string or the name of the n-th parameter
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: parstr ( ring name ) | parstr ( int expression ) | parstr ( ring name, int expression ). Type: string. If ring name omitted basering used. Examples: parstr(r) -> 'a,b,c'; parstr(2)-> 'b'; parstr(r,3) -> 'c'. See charstr, npars, ordstr, ring, varstr.

rubrics_metrics.name: preimage
rubrics_metrics.description: returns the source ring of a map or returns the preimage of an ideal under a given map
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: preimage ( map ) | preimage ( ring name, map name, ideal name ) | preimage ( ring name, ideal expression, ideal name ). Type: ring or ideal. Notes: second argument must be a map from basering to given ring (or ideal defining such map), and ideal must be in the given ring. Important: preimage handles ideals (not polynomials) — preimage of a principal ideal is the closure of the preimage of the ideal, not of the polynomial. Examples show computing kernel via preimage and kernel commands. See ideal, kernel, map, ring.

rubrics_metrics.name: prime
rubrics_metrics.description: returns the largest prime less than or equal to the argument; returns 2 for all arguments smaller than 3
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: prime ( int expression ). Type: int. Examples: prime(320000) -> 319993; prime(32004) -> 32003; prime(0) or prime(-1) -> 2. See general lib and int.

rubrics_metrics.name: primefactors
rubrics_metrics.description: returns the prime factorisation (list) up to an optional bound on prime factors; works on int/bigint/number expressions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: primefactors ( int/bigint/number expression ) or primefactors ( ..., int expression ). Type: list. Purpose: returns prime factors possibly up to bound b; when called with numbers, they are assumed integers in polynomial ring over Q. Returned list structure: L[1][i] = i-th prime factor (ascending), L[2][i] = multiplicity of factor, L[3] = remainder n'. Examples show factoring a bigint power product and factoring with bound. See prime.

rubrics_metrics.name: print
rubrics_metrics.description: prints the expression or returns formatted string representations; supports printing graded Betti numbers via second form print(expression,'betti') and custom format strings
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: print ( expression ), print ( expression, 'betti' ), print ( expression, format string ). Type: string. Purpose: first form prints expression; second prints graded Betti numbers from a matrix; third returns printed output as string per format. Supported format strings: '%s' (string(expression)), '%2s' (like %s but insert newlines after every comma), '%l' (type-braced form suitable for copy/paste), '%2l' (like %l but with newlines), '%;' (string equivalent to typing expression), '%t' (string equivalent to typing type expression), '%p' (string equivalent to typing print(expression)), '%b' (string equivalent to print(expression,'betti')). Examples show printing modules, building strings s=print(m,'%s'), print(m,'%2s'), print(m,'%l'), print with 'betti' on intmat M=betti(mres(m,0)). Also shows printing lists and composition. See mres, betti, module, list.
